_info: Dataset registry for the fence detector. Every dataset is synthetic and auto-labelled from Gazebo ground truth by tools/make_dataset.py (no hand labels). Images are not in git: they live on the training machine under ~/querra-data/<id> and can be regenerated with the command at the given code commit. Farm seed = --seed + layout number (default --seed 100), so layout 40 is always seed 140. Ids are the folder names. 'role' says how a split may be used: train, val (model selection) or test (never used for training or model selection).

datasets.style: v1
datasets.notes: Random farms: fence shape, post spacing, wire heights, 2-3 broken wires, 1-2 fallen posts, 1-2 branches, herd, sun, grass colour. Camera 5-20 m, tilt 35-80 deg. The dead strand after a break is always grey.

datasets.style: v2
datasets.command: tools/make_dataset.sh --style v2 (layouts 20-29, 300 frames; tests: layouts 40-42, 250 frames; --mission-world layout 90, 400 frames)
datasets.notes: Targets the false broken wire: 3-4 breaks per farm, so long dead strands, drawn in random colours (grey, live yellow, dull, dark) and labelled wire. Three break shapes. 60% of the poses imitate the inspection flight.

The test farms use the same seeds as fence_yolo_v2's test, so the two looks are compared on the same farms and pose distribution (not frame-identical: empty frames are skipped).

datasets.style: ground robot side camera
datasets.notes: Test frames were written as G00-G02 at 54f574b (the same names as training layouts 0-2, in another folder) and renamed T00-T02; the generator names test layouts T since the next commit. Random forest enclosures in the style of forest.json (6-9 sided fence, 3.5-5.5 m post spacing, 3-5 broken wires, 2-3 fallen posts, 2-3 branches on the wires, forest density and sun randomised). The camera is a free copy of the ground robot's side camera (640x400, 100 deg hfov) at robot poses: 1.4-2.5 m outside the fence, 0.70 m up, looking left and 6 deg down, with heading, pitch and roll noise. 45% of the poses are near a fault (each fault type equally often). Labels from the known geometry with the drone's 7 classes; a depth camera on the same mount removes hidden parts; nothing farther than 12 m. About a third of the frames without a fault are dropped. No animals in the forest.

datasets.notes: The real forest.json world along the robot's patrol route, one frame every 0.5 m at the nominal camera pose (no noise), with patrol_poses.jsonl and patrol_faults.json (F1-F5). Never used for training or model selection: tools/ground_patrol_eval.py scores faults found and false alerts on it (5 of 8 frames confirm an alert).

datasets.notes: No farm fence in any photo: every fault box is a false alarm, and every cow or sheep box too. 1,229 photos show cables (10,103 outlined), 271 wooden poles (333). datasets.style: photos of electric fences from Wikimedia Commons, free licences, 1280 px wide
datasets.license: per photo, in manifest.json: public domain, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA (most: CC BY-SA 2.0, geograph.org.uk); credit the authors when showing a photo
datasets.command: tools/fetch_commons.py ~/querra-data/real/commons_fences --depth 3 --cat 'Pasture electric fences' --cat 'Electric fences by country' --cat 'Electric fences' --cat 'Electric fence insulators' --exclude border --exclude auschwitz --exclude camp --exclude gobi --exclude gardina --exclude 'wire of death' --exclude sign --exclude prison --exclude 'berlin wall' --exclude 'iron curtain' --exclude military --exclude missile --exclude holocaust --exclude concentration --exclude ghetto --exclude nazi --exclude 'de gas' --exclude 'gas chamber' --width 1280; ~/.querra-train-venv/bin/python tools/label_drafts.py draft ~/querra-data/real/commons_fences/images --model ~/querra-data/models/ground-yolo11n-v0.3.pt --out ~/querra-data/real/commons_fences_set
datasets.notes: 467 photos pass the licence and exclusion checks (one more was taken out by hand: a concentration camp photo filed under electric fences). Wikimedia throttles the download to about one a minute, so it fills over hours; label_drafts.py draft adds the new ones. Mostly eye-level landscapes from the UK, the Czech Republic and the Alps; about a third show a fence close enough to label. Labelled in ~/querra-data/real/commons_fences_set (docs/labelling.md); a photo with no usable fence is skipped there, so the test set will be smaller. Real images stay out of git.

datasets.style: v4 (inspection-flight poses), real fence conductors (polytape, polyrope, steel wire, polywire), 3x supersampled
datasets.command: tools/make_dataset.sh --seed 100 --look classic --style v4 --start 250 --layouts 256 --split train --frames 250 --supersample 3 --fence-look polytape,polyrope,steel,polywire --no-wire-labels steel,polywire --out ~/querra-data/drone_yolo_looks (rich: --look rich --start 256 --layouts 262; val: --look classic --start 262 --layouts 264 --split val --fence-look polyrope,polytape)
datasets.notes: Real conductors for model-v0.6: new farms flown at the measured flight poses (as fence_yolo_flight_*), with the strands drawn at their real size (sim/gen_world.py FENCE_LOOKS) and the colour camera rendered at 3x and averaged in linear light. The look cycles by layout number: train 750 frames each of steel wire (2.5 mm grey; 500 classic, 250 rich), polywire (3 mm yellow; 500, 250), polytape (40 mm white; 250, 500) and polyrope (6 mm white; 250, 500); val 250 polyrope, 250 polytape (classic). Steel-wire and polywire layouts have no wire or wire_break boxes (--no-wire-labels): from 11 m the wire is a tenth of a pixel, so the model is not asked to find it; their posts, fallen posts, branches and animals are labelled as usual, and the poses are the same as with the labels. Labels, train: post 8926, wire 5111, wire_break 419, fallen_post 287, branch 273, cow 528, sheep 399; val: post 1397, wire 1615, wire_break 100, fallen_post 52, branch 29, cow 79, sheep 55.
